subject: using my pdf with others' data

messages.author: 0a4327e4a03ff62a
messages.subject: using my pdf with others' data
parts:
Hello group.
I received several data of observations (hooded crows) from line
transects, but I absolutely don't trust the way the operators
recorded the distances (they were many different operators, some of
them with a laser rangefinder, some of them without).
I have a detection function for the same species in the same study
area, built on data that I personally collected the last two years, so
my question is the following: would it be correct if I use "their"
encounter rate combined with "my" detection function to estimate the
density? I mean, is there some moral or methodological
controindication?
Thank you in advance!
Luca

messages.author: 6e15de0134e98c08
messages.subject: Re: using my pdf with others' data
parts:
Hi Luca,

What you are doing is replacing data by an assumption, and obviously,=20
that only makes sense if the assumption holds. In this case, the=20
assumption is that the detection function of the operators is the same=20
as yours. But given that you seem to be more careful and perhaps have=20
more experience than the operators, that might not be the case anyway.

And the problem is, really, that assumption is based on faith, as there=20
is no way to test it. So..., you can do it, but it comes at a price.

Cheers

Tiago

I think I'll try to use all the data to build a detection function
with 'operator' as a covariate... then I'll try to do another estimate
using only my pdf... and I'll see what happen...

Luca
